items.title: tool-description token budget
items.basis: The r2 review marked this needs-decision. It is now settled: DECISIONS-r3.md Q13 sets a hard 1,024-char cap per tool description, enforced by lint. docs/v2/prompt/lint.mjs:19 implements this exactly: `r.chars > 1024` (2048 for the 'instructions' block). ADR-0005 cites PR7 for the same number. The r2 verdict is superseded; no further action needed.

archaeology.note: Not a v1 behaviour change; budget is a new v2 lint rule, no prior commit to trace.

items.title: Codex external-file settings
items.basis: Still has zero doc coverage: grep for 'external-file', '944' and 'config.toml' across PRD-v2.md, docs/v2/README.md, docs/v2/TECH-SPEC.md and all ADRs returns nothing. Q11 (project source per host) talks about Codex as a host but does not cover how v2 reads Codex's own settings file. v1 handled Codex settings as a file on disk (config.toml), with repeated fixes for plugin-root and marketplace drift.

archaeology.INTRODUCED_BY: 75ae6ae3 feat: multi-platform adapters, session continuity, hook scripts (v1, cm-main)
archaeology.ORIGINAL_INTENT: read Codex settings from its own config file on disk rather than from context-mode's own config
archaeology.REGRESSION_RISK: if v2 does not pin how/when it reads this external file, repeat of v1's plugin-root drift bugs (98d239b7 fix(codex): resolve plugin-manager root for doctor and upgrade (#771); 2a38f833 Fix Codex plugin-root drift diagnostics)
archaeology.SAFE_FIX_CONSTRAINTS: one documented read path for the external Codex settings file, no fallback chain (owner decision), covered by a GP7 or new GP row

items.fix: Add one ADR line (or extend ADR-0007/0011) stating where/when v2 reads the Codex external settings file, then a contract-test row.

items.title: Opt-in retrieval-only mode, per-agent activation, scoped indexing (OpenCode)
items.basis: Confirmed still uncovered: grep for 'retrieval-only', 'opt-in' + 'index', 'scoped index' across all v2 docs and ADRs returns no hits. This is a new feature request, not a v1 regression, so MUST-5 archaeology does not apply (no prior v1 code implements it). It needs an explicit scope call (in-scope for v2.0, or deferred) before it can be closed either way; right now it is simply unaddressed.
items.evidence: grep -rn -i 'retrieval-only|opt-in.*index|scoped index' docs/v2/*.md docs/v2/adr/*.md -> no hits (checked 2026-10-14)
items.fix: Owner must say yes/no/deferred for v2.0 scope; if yes, needs its own ADR and GP row.
